Some see an opportunity to control others. Hiro wants an adventure; Claire wants room to decide who she is. Twenty years of superhero television have produced bigger images and more elaborate worlds, but this show's first season still understands the nervous excitement of discovering you might be different. Its question has aged well: once you can do something remarkable, what responsibility follows? Heroes works because it makes that question personal before anyone gets to call themselves a hero.

title: Who Is a Football Club For? What Ted Lasso and Manchester City Reveal About Ownership
description: Ted Lasso trusts a good owner to protect football. Manchester City's financial ruling asks what happens when trust is not enough.
body: In Ted Lasso 's third season, Edwin Akufo gathers club owners to sell them a lucrative new league. Rebecca Welton looks around the room and asks them to remember the people who first made them love football. Her argument works. The other owners abandon the scheme, and the game is saved from their worst instincts by one of their own. It is an appealing scene, especially because Rebecca once treated AFC Richmond as a tool for hurting her ex-husband. She has learned to care about the club and the people around it. Still, the decision happens in a room full of owners. Supporters are central to Rebecca's argument, but none of them gets a seat at the table. The club is theirs in feeling and hers in law. That gap between belonging and control is where Ted Lasso has something to say about real football. Manchester City's newly published financial ruling makes the limits of the show's answer easier to see. Richmond and City are not equivalent clubs, and Edwin Akufo's fictional league has nothing to do with the charges against City. The connection is the power that ownership gives someone over a competition other people have built their lives around. Spoilers for Ted Lasso through season three follow. Rebecca's change is the point In the pilot, Rebecca hires Ted because she expects him to fail. Richmond's staff, players and fans face the consequences of a plan they know nothing about. Her ownership gives her the freedom to try it. As the series continues, Ted helps create a culture in which players support each other and staff members are heard. Rebecca begins to value that culture herself. The season-three episode "International Break" takes her change beyond Richmond. Akufo's proposal promises wealth and influence to a select group of owners. Rebecca recognizes that a competition built for them could leave the people who fill the stands with much less to believe in. She persuades the room by reminding her peers that they were once fans too. It is a fine character moment. It is also a very Ted Lasso solution: a person with power looks at other people more generously, then uses that power well. By the end of the third season, Rebecca even offers Richmond supporters a share of the club. Her change of heart matters, but she still chooses the terms on which they can participate. A real club has no writer to make the owner listen Manchester City has a different history and vastly different resources. City Football Group says it is majority owned through a company wholly owned by Sheikh Mansour, with Silver Lake holding a substantial minority stake. City's investment has helped build a club with global reach and success on the pitch. It has also made questions about financial reporting consequential for competitors who have to play under the same rules. On 29 September 2026, the Premier League published the findings of an independent commission . It upheld all substantive charges concerning breaches of financial rules from 2009/10 through 2017/18, as well as three of four charges concerning failure to cooperate with the league's investigation. The commission found that sham arrangements overstated revenue and understated costs by more than £900 million, giving the appearance that City complied with spending limits when it did not. City maintains its innocence and says it will appeal . A sanction has not yet been imposed. This is a question about accounts, oversight and competitive rules. It cannot tell us how much a City supporter loves the club, or dismiss the work of players and staff. It also cannot be resolved by asking whether the owner feels an emotional connection to football. The league has to establish what happened and enforce its rules through a process that can withstand challenge. Football's invisible decisions Ted Lasso makes club administration visible through Rebecca and Higgins. They have names and faces, so we can see when a decision hurts someone and when another decision begins to repair it. Real administration often consists of contracts, accounts and regulatory proceedings. It shapes what clubs can spend, who can compete and whether other clubs trust the result. The City process shows how difficult accountability can be after the fact. The league says its investigation began in December 2018; the commission hearing ended in December 2024, and its core findings were published in September 2026. City has the right to appeal and the question of sanction remains open. Whatever follows, those seasons cannot be played again. That delay matters to City's supporters as well as its rivals, all of whom have had to live with the unresolved case. Richmond's pub regulars remind us why any of this has stakes. A club is part of how people spend their weeks and remember their lives. City's fans have that relationship with their team too. Ownership can fund a stadium, recruit talent and take a club across the world, but those decisions do not give owners a greater claim to its meaning than the people who have stayed with it. The part television cannot settle Rebecca's speech is moving because it imagines someone powerful remembering what it felt like to have no power in the game. More owners could stand to remember that. But the scene ends when the owners agree. It has little reason to ask what happens when they do not, or when a decision is hidden in financial paperwork for years. That is why the City ruling belongs in this conversation without turning City into Ted Lasso 's villain. The commission's findings, City's appeal and the eventual sanction need to be judged on their own evidence. Richmond supplies a question worth bringing to that process: who pays for the choices made at the top of a club? The real answer has to be written into rules and enforced in time for the people outside the owners' room to trust them.

title: Warcraft: where to start
description: Where to start Warcraft, what to skip, and the characters and events worth knowing before you play.
body: Choose the adventure you want. The strategy campaigns, modern MMO, and Classic offer different ways into the same world. You can enjoy any of them without completing decades of games. Warcraft I and II, WoW, novels, and comics. Read their short recaps only if you become curious. This is a strategy game with armies and missions. It introduces the world through its leaders rather than a custom adventurer. Play The Frozen Throne next. Stop there for a complete strategy-era journey, or follow one character into WoW. Modern World of Warcraft I want an MMO I can join today The current new-player experience teaches your class and leads through a modern introduction. You can reach today’s shared adventure without clearing every old zone or raid. Start with the new-player path offered in game, including Dragonflight where directed. Alliance and Horde are coalitions; Azeroth faces threats larger than either. Clearing old expansions in release order, collecting everything, and buying lore books. The MMO tells stories across quests, cinematics, and raids. Old campaigns are not one seamless sequence, and access to the latest expansion is separate from learning the world. Join Midnight when your character is ready. Use the saga recap below; choose The War Within first if you want the arc’s beginning. Their recaps supply the relevant bridge. This is still WoW: character requirements and campaign access apply. A lore entry point is not a promise that a fresh character can immediately enter every quest. Follow the main campaign, then Midnight. Return to older regions only when their stories interest you. World of Warcraft Classic I want to discover a world slowly Local quests and travel let you learn Azeroth through your own adventurer. Prior knowledge of Warcraft III is useful, but unnecessary. The factions are rebuilding after major wars. Pick a race and class that interest you and learn their home region. Strategy games, modern expansion campaigns, and a checklist of raids. Classic’s rules and pace differ from modern WoW. Choose the Classic version your friends play; it is not a required first step before retail. title: Dragon Age: where to start
description: Where to start Dragon Age, why each entry point works, what to skip, and the lore and characters worth knowing.
body: Each major Dragon Age game introduces a new protagonist. Start with the style of adventure you want, then learn the older decisions that matter to its people. Choose Origins for the richest introduction to Thedas’s institutions, Inquisition for a broad modern adventure, or The Veilguard for a more direct action RPG. None requires a full series marathon. title: Gears of War: where to start

body: Gears works best when you care about the squad. Its original trilogy, later generation, and prequels offer different beginnings without requiring novels or competitive play. The first two games, the books, television seasons, and collecting every map marker. Some returning relationships and political references assume a shared past. The optional recap reveals earlier game outcomes, and imported or simulated choices can affect details. Finish the main story, then Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. The 2026 remaster is a version of this campaign, not a fourth chapter. The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings I want a shorter political adventure Its focused chapters put alliances and consequences at the centre. It is a workable starting point for players more interested in political choices than a vast open world. Geralt is caught in the aftermath of attacks on northern rulers. The first game and the novels if you prefer to learn through this adventure. Combat and navigation are less forgiving than The Witcher 3. A major route choice means one playthrough will not show every chapter. Continue to Wild Hunt when you want a broader world and the Ciri storyline. Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales I want a self-contained ruler’s story Queen Meve’s campaign introduces the world through leadership, war, and difficult decisions. Geralt’s trilogy is not its prerequisite. Meve leads the northern kingdoms of Lyria and Rivia during Nilfgaard’s invasion. All three Geralt games, competitive Gwent, and the television series. Its battles use a card system rather than the trilogy’s action combat. It is a different protagonist’s adventure. Try Wild Hunt if you want to explore the same world through Geralt. title: Metal Gear: where to start
description: Where to start Metal Gear, why each entry point works, what to skip, and the lore and characters worth knowing.
body: Metal Gear combines military thrillers, family connections, and arguments about loyalty and control. Its prequels explain earlier history after the audience has already met its consequences, so chronological order is not automatically the best first route. Start Metal Gear Solid for the central Solid Snake story, then follow release order. Choose Metal Gear Solid 3 or its Delta remake for an accessible, largely self-contained Cold War prequel. Metal Gear Solid I want the central story and its surprises Shadow Moses introduces Snake, his support team, and the series’ mix of stealth and political intrigue in one focused mission. Optional recaps cover the two MSX games. A veteran operative is sent to resolve a hostage crisis involving a nuclear threat. Playing the two older Metal Gear games, every codec conversation, and the prequels before starting. Its controls and camera reflect its era. The older games add history, but the briefing and recap can provide enough context. Continue Metal Gear Solid 2, then 3, then 4. Follow with Peace Walker, Ground Zeroes, and The Phantom Pain if Big Boss’s story interests you. Metal Gear Solid 3 / Delta: Snake Eater I want a focused espionage prequel A Cold War mission introduces its own cast and emotional conflict. Delta retells this campaign with newer presentation. Naked Snake is operating in 1964 amid a crisis involving the Soviet Union, a weapon project, and his mentor. The earlier released games before this adventure. Starting with the prequel changes how later connections land. Avoid online character biographies, which often reveal their entire future. Return to Metal Gear Solid and continue release order. Alternatively follow the Big Boss-era games after accepting that you are seeing history before its later reveals. The Phantom Pain I mainly want open-ended stealth missions Its flexible bases and tools make it a strong gameplay-first entry, even when the wider conspiracy is not your immediate interest. An independent military organisation has been devastated; its survivors seek to rebuild and pursue those responsible. A complete saga marathon and optional collectible recordings. Its narrative depends on Peace Walker and Ground Zeroes, and important context sits outside the missions. It is a weaker first choice if story clarity matters most. Read the optional bridge recap, then play missions at your own pace. Try Snake Eater or Metal Gear Solid afterwards for a more concentrated narrative. title: The Legend of Zelda: where to start
description: Where to start The Legend of Zelda, why each entry point works, what to skip, and the lore and characters worth knowing.
body: Most Zelda games introduce a new adventure with familiar names and themes. Their historical connections are optional context, not a requirement to work through every incarnation of Link before choosing one. Start Breath of the Wild for open-ended exploration, Link’s Awakening for a compact traditional adventure, or Ocarina of Time for the classic 3D structure. Echoes of Wisdom offers a welcoming adventure led by Zelda herself. Breath of the Wild I want freedom and discovery Its world teaches through exploration and experimentation. Local people and optional memories provide context without requiring earlier games. Hyrule is living in the aftermath of a calamity, and Link must decide how to confront the danger still present. Every earlier Zelda, collecting every shrine or seed, and a timeline explanation. Its open structure is different from the older item-and-dungeon pattern. The story is partly discovered out of order. Continue to Tears of the Kingdom if you want more of this Link and Zelda. Hyrule Warriors stories are optional. Link’s Awakening I want a compact, traditional adventure A self-contained island mystery introduces Zelda-style dungeons and tools without requiring knowledge of Hyrule’s royal history. Link washes ashore on Koholint and searches for a way home. The earlier games, their lore, and a branch-by-branch marathon. Its smaller world and older puzzle structure are less open-ended than Breath of the Wild. The original and remake tell the same central story. Try A Link to the Past or A Link Between Worlds for a larger top-down adventure. Ocarina of Time I want the classic 3D adventure A focused opening, expanding tools, and memorable companions introduce the series’ traditional 3D pattern. It also supplies useful context for later branch discussions. A boy from the forest is drawn into Hyrule’s struggle over sacred power. The earlier released games and learning the official timeline before playing. Camera, combat, and presentation depend on the edition. Its centrality to the timeline does not make it compulsory for newer games. Choose Majora’s Mask for this Link’s direct follow-up, or The Wind Waker and Twilight Princess for different later branches. Echoes of Wisdom I want to play as Zelda Its new central mechanic offers inventive solutions in a compact top-down Hyrule. A fresh crisis introduces its own supporting cast. Strange rifts threaten the kingdom; Zelda works with a companion called Tri. Earlier Zelda games, playing as Link first, and knowing its precise timeline position. Echo-based problem solving differs from the usual sword-first approach. Familiar geography is a bonus rather than a prerequisite. Try Link’s Awakening for another compact adventure or Breath of the Wild for a larger playground. Link Zelda Ganon / Ganondorf Impa Skull Kid Tetra Vaati Midna Fi Rauru of the distant era Sidon

title: Tomb Raider: where to start
description: Where to start Tomb Raider, how its eras connect, and the people, relics and rivalries behind Lara Croft’s adventures.
body: Tomb Raider follows an archaeologist whose curiosity takes her into places that should have stayed buried. Some games celebrate her confidence; others ask what it costs to become that person. Choose one era first. You do not need three versions of her life as homework. Start Tomb Raider (2013) for a character-led origin, or Legend for an already confident Lara and a shorter globe-trotting adventure. Choose the first game in I–III Remastered if discovering the series’ original tombs appeals to you. Each is a complete way in. Tomb Raider (2013) I want a modern origin and a close look at Lara A first expedition introduces Lara and her friends as people rather than names you should already know. Its survival story gives her later determination an emotional foundation. Lara is a young archaeologist aboard the Endurance. An expedition searching for Yamatai becomes a struggle to get home. All earlier games, the films, comics and animated series. Collectibles and optional tombs are not prerequisites. Combat and cinematic peril take more space than the older games’ slow exploration. Expect a grittier Lara than the confident figure on the classic covers. Continue with Rise of the Tomb Raider, then Shadow of the Tomb Raider. Stop after this game if a single adventure is enough. Tomb Raider: Legend I want confident Lara, puzzles and globe-trotting Its guided opening, fluid movement and supporting cast make a welcoming introduction to the adventurer at work. A personal mystery gives the journey a clear direction. Lara investigates an ancient sword and a mystery connected to her mother. Her team helps remotely; the game introduces them. The six classic games, the Survivor trilogy and reading a family history in advance. Older camera conventions and quick-time events may take adjustment. The central family mystery continues into Underworld. Play Anniversary for this era’s earlier Scion adventure, then Underworld for the convergence. Release order is our recommendation; Anniversary → Legend → Underworld is the era’s broad story order. Tomb Raider (1996), in I–III Remastered I want the original exploration and atmosphere The first adventure lets architecture, silence and dangerous spaces carry the experience. Start with its first game rather than treating the collection as a three-game obligation. Lara accepts a commission to retrieve an ancient artifact called the Scion. Her employer and the relic’s history are part of the mystery. II and III until you want more, the expansions, the later classic games and both reboot trilogies. Navigation and precise platforming ask for patience. The remaster offers control choices, but the underlying level design remains from the original era. Try Tomb Raider II for another mostly standalone relic hunt. Continue into The Last Revelation later if you want the Von Croy story; III is an optional expedition. Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light I want a self-contained adventure with a friend An isometric action-puzzle adventure puts cooperation at the centre. It also works as a solo detour without a larger continuity commitment. Lara and the ancient warrior Totec must deal with a dangerous power released from the Mirror of Smoke. Every mainline game, Lara’s family mysteries and completing all challenge objectives. Its viewpoint and emphasis differ from the main games. It gives you Lara’s adventure spirit rather than a detailed origin or ongoing character arc. Try Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris for another co-op detour. Choose Legend or Tomb Raider (2013) when you want a mainline story. title: Assassin’s Creed: where to start
description: Where to start Assassin’s Creed, which stories connect, and the lore, motives and relationships worth knowing.
body: Assassin’s Creed follows people whose private struggles become entangled with a secret war over freedom and control. The historical adventure is usually your way in; the Animus and modern-day story explain why someone is revisiting it. Choose a person or period first, then deepen the connections that interest you. Begin Assassin’s Creed II for Ezio’s character arc, Origins for an Egyptian open-world RPG, or Mirage for a more focused stealth adventure. Black Flag is a welcoming pirate route; Shadows offers a fresh pair of protagonists in Japan. Historical chronology is optional context, not our recommended first-play order. Assassin’s Creed II I want a character I can grow with Ezio learns about the conflict as you do. His family, friendships and changing responsibilities make the larger conspiracy personal. A young Florentine is drawn into a violent conspiracy. The modern framing follows Desmond, who has escaped an organization using his inherited memories. Playing the original first if you mainly want Ezio’s life. The short films, collectibles and side games are optional. II continues Desmond’s situation from the first game. You can follow Ezio without every detail, but start the 2007 game instead if the present-day mystery matters most. Continue Brotherhood, then Revelations. III follows the modern-day story with a new historical protagonist; it is not a fourth Ezio game. Assassin’s Creed Origins I want exploration and the Brotherhood’s beginnings Bayek and Aya’s personal loss gives the formation of an organization a human cause. Ancient Egypt provides a distinct setting and the RPG structure offers room to explore. Bayek is a protector in Egypt. He and his wife Aya pursue the people behind a devastating family loss. All earlier games, knowing the whole Isu history, clearing every map marker, and buying every expansion. This is a larger RPG with levels and equipment. The historical story begins fresh, while Layla introduces another continuing modern-day thread. The Hidden Ones is an optional follow-up about the organization taking shape. Choose Odyssey, then Valhalla in release order if you want more of Layla’s thread. Assassin’s Creed Mirage I want stealth in a focused city adventure Basim’s apprenticeship teaches the Hidden Ones’ methods through investigations, tools and a close view of Baghdad. A street thief with troubling visions dreams of joining the Hidden Ones. Roshan becomes his mentor. Valhalla before beginning this historical coming-of-age story, the older games and a complete artifact glossary. The ending gains extra meaning from Valhalla. Mirage works as an introduction to Basim, but choose Valhalla first if preserving its revelations is your priority. Explore the optional Valley of Memory story if you want more Basim. Choose Valhalla for his later role, or II for another apprentice-to-mentor arc. Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag / Black Flag Resynced I want pirates, exploration and a flawed hero Edward enters the conflict from the outside, making his ambitions and friendships a useful introduction to what the Brotherhood asks of a person. Edward Kenway wants wealth and independence in the Caribbean. His shortcuts draw him into the Assassin–Templar conflict. III before Edward’s adventure, playing both editions, and completing every naval activity. The original contains a post-III modern framing and may reveal earlier series outcomes. Resynced reworks the experience; the modern-day release route in this guide uses the original. Freedom Cry follows Adéwalé in a separate, optional story. Rogue and III explore the later Atlantic conflict; play III after the earlier Desmond games if following that modern-day arc. Assassin’s Creed Shadows I want a new cast and contrasting perspectives Naoe and Yasuke offer different relationships to power and different ways through the same turbulent setting. You meet their local allies and opponents within the game. Naoe is a shinobi from Iga; Yasuke is a samurai whose path intersects hers during Japan’s wars of unification. Every earlier historical adventure, DLC before the base story, and knowing all previous Assassins by name. Its dual protagonists and larger systems differ from Mirage’s concentrated stealth approach. Shared-world references add context but need not dictate your starting point. Claws of Awaji is an optional continuation after the base story. Try Mirage for a smaller stealth route or Origins for another large historical world. title: Final Fantasy: where to start
description: Where to start Final Fantasy, which stories connect, and the lore, motives and relationships worth knowing.
body: Final Fantasy is a family of worlds, not one story running from I to XVI. Familiar creatures, magic and names invite recognition, while most numbered games introduce new people and histories. Pick the kind of journey you want, then follow that world’s relationships and conflicts. Start X for a clear, turn-based journey into an unfamiliar culture, IX for storybook fantasy with thoughtful characters, or XVI for action and a darker political world. VI is an excellent pixel-era choice. VII Remake begins a connected modern project; it is not a replacement that contains the entire 1997 story. Final Fantasy X I want turn-based combat and a clear story Tidus enters Spira as an outsider, so the world explains itself alongside him. The pilgrimage gives you a focused route through people, places and beliefs. Sin threatens Spira. Yuna is a summoner undertaking a pilgrimage, and Tidus becomes one of her companions. I–IX, every optional boss, and X-2 until you want to stay in this world. Its linear journey and deliberate battles differ from open-world RPGs. Some optional challenges are far more demanding than the main story. Choose X-2 only after X if you want more of Yuna and Spira. It changes tone and combat; you can finish X and stop. Final Fantasy IX I want warm fantasy with serious questions A theatre troupe, a princess and a young mage offer an inviting opening. Their worries about identity, belonging and duty grow out of the adventure rather than a lore lecture. Zidane’s troupe visits Alexandria, where Garnet’s concerns and Vivi’s unexpected involvement bring them together. Every other Final Fantasy, a glossary of recurring monsters, and optional completion challenges. Its older battle pace and presentation may require adjustment. The playful look does not mean every part of the story is lighthearted. VI offers another ensemble story about power and identity; X offers a more directed pilgrimage. Neither is a continuation you must play. Final Fantasy VII Remake I want a modern cast and action with tactical choices Midgar gives Cloud’s party a strong local beginning. Their competing motives make the conflict with Shinra understandable before the larger mysteries widen. Cloud accepts work with Avalanche, a group opposing a company that draws energy from the planet. I–VI, the 1997 game before beginning, Crisis Core as compulsory homework, and the films or mobile games. This is the first part of a connected reimagining, not the entire original VII. Familiar material develops differently; first-time players may find some late mysteries deliberately unresolved. Continue Rebirth. Intergrade is an expanded edition of Remake, and its INTERmission episode is an optional Yuffie detour before Rebirth. The project’s final announced chapter is future orientation here. Choose original VII instead if you want the complete original story in one game. Final Fantasy VI, including Pixel Remaster I want the pixel-era ensemble and its lore Different people reveal different costs of imperial power. A relatively compact visual style makes its towns, character scenes and escalating conflict easy to read. An empire turns rediscovered magic into military power. Terra’s place in that system is the opening question. I–V, buying the whole Pixel Remaster collection, and finding every secret before advancing. It uses older navigation and timed command battles. There is no single protagonist whose route substitutes for the whole ensemble. Try IV for a more focused redemption story, or IX for another cast wrestling with belonging. Each begins afresh. Final Fantasy XVI I want action combat and a darker political story Clive’s family bonds and the treatment of people with magic give its wars concrete human stakes. The game introduces its own vocabulary and nations. Valisthea’s nations depend on powerful crystals. Certain people wield Eikons, while others are exploited for magical ability. All earlier Final Fantasy games, understanding every summon before playing, and the expansions before the base adventure. It focuses on one directly controlled fighter rather than turn-based party management. Violence and adult themes make it a different tone from IX. Echoes of the Fallen and The Rising Tide are optional additions with late-game requirements. XV offers a separate action-oriented road trip with a stronger traveling-party emphasis. Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn I want a long story in an online world Your own adventurer grows into a central role while recurring allies give an expanding world continuity. Start with the main scenario rather than treating years of updates as an immediate obligation. Begin as an adventurer in Eorzea. Main Scenario Quests introduce the institutions, companions and conflicts you need. I–XIII, the retired original XIV release, XI, raids and other optional activities until they interest you. It is a substantial online commitment with multiplayer elements. Account, trial and subscription conditions vary; check the official options before choosing an edition. Continue the main scenario through Heavensward → Stormblood → Shadowbringers → Endwalker → Dawntrail as your interest grows. Finishing a chapter is a reasonable stopping point; the guide does not require catching up to every patch.
